dimensions.assessment: Affects job applicants seeking federal cybersecurity positions and federal agencies hiring for information technology management or cybersecurity roles.
dimensions.evidence: any position in the competitive service classified under the GS-2210 information technology management series

dimensions.assessment: Restricts agencies from setting minimum educational prerequisites for certain technical jobs unless required by law.
dimensions.evidence: an agency may prescribe a minimum educational requirement for employment in such a position only if a minimum education qualification is required by law

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state any fiscal or budgetary impacts.
Amends title 5, United States Code, to alter federal hiring standards and require OPM publication of qualification data.
dimensions.evidence: Section 3308 of title 5, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent restrictions on federal hiring practices alongside annual OPM reporting.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter, the Office of Personnel Management shall publish on the Office's website

missing_information: Data on the exact number of federal positions impacted or potential recruitment cost changes.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill limits educational requirements and qualifications used by federal agencies when evaluating candidates for specific cybersecurity positions in the competitive service.
